item.title: Topological Transitions of Evanescent Waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.07038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the band structure of evanescent waves, that is, the decaying or growing solutions that live within the gaps of tight-binding Hamiltonians. Although the underlying Hamiltonian is Hermitian, these modes carry complex wavevectors and therefore exhibit a non-Hermitian dispersion. Using the transfer matrix formalism in one dimension, we show that, in addition to the standard exceptional points that appear at the band edges, a different type of exceptional point can arise inside the gap, protected by spinless time-reversal symmetry. Tuning model parameters drives a topological transition where such in-gap exceptional points are nucleated in pairs, mediated by a crossing between purely imaginary momentum branches. We show that this spectral structure is diagnosed by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index assigned to every energy inside the gap, with the in-gap exceptional points arising as its domain walls. A generic bound state in the system has a tail that is purely exponential when its energy lies between a band edge and the nearest exceptional point, but becomes oscillatory - with a wavevector differing from the band-edge momentum - when its energy lies between the pair of in-gap exceptional points. We illustrate these results using continuum and tight-binding models, as well as an anisotropic photonic crystal.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Pavez, Tom Sheppard, Yoonseok Hwang, Hannah M. Price, Frank Schindler

item.title: Parity-Selective Quantum Interference in Unconventional Magnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting has emerged as a defining feature of unconventional magnetic states. Here we show that quantum interference offers a symmetry-resolved probe for the parity of such spin splitting, as even- and odd-parity magnets exhibit qualitatively different weak (anti-)localization behaviors. Even-parity magnets can host time-reversal symmetric scattering loops depicted by the spin group, giving rise to a weak localization that can be suppressed by spin-orbit coupling. In contrast, odd-parity magnets have a hidden weak antilocalization that can be released by spinorbit coupling. We further derive the corresponding magnetoconductivity formulas to facilitate experimental explorations. Our results not only advance the weak (anti-)localization theory to unconventional magnets but also suggest a practical diagnostic of unconventional spin-split magnetic states.
item.dc:creator: Yiyuan Chen, Xiao-Bin Qiang, Hai-Zhou Lu, Congjun Wu, X. C. Xie

item.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.07434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/{\pi} phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.
item.dc:creator: Chongzhou Wang, Zhengda Jing, Weichao Yu

item.title: Supermoir\'e Formation and Robust Topological Edge State in Helical Trilayer Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.07435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When two materials with nearly matched lattice constants meet, they form commensurate domains separated by incommensurate domain walls that absorb the mismatch. Recently, this picture has been extended to moir\'e lattices: when two moir\'e superlattices have nearly equal periodicities, they can form a "supermoir\'e" consisting of commensurate moir\'e domains separated by domain walls. Helical trilayer graphene (HTG) is a particularly interesting example: theory predicts that its commensurate domains are distinct topological insulators, separated by a network of conducting domain walls. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to visualize supermoir\'e domains and their electronic properties in HTG at a twist angle of $\sim1.7^\circ$. We find atomic-scale evidence of relaxation into supermoir\'e domains, each hosting flat bands separated from remote bands by large gaps of $\sim40$ meV. Domain walls exhibit spectrally uniform edge states along their length, in excellent agreement with calculations for valley-protected topological edge modes. The topological character of the flat bands is intimately tied to wavefunction localization on a graphene sublattice, and we reveal the topological change across a domain boundary by imaging the reversal of sublattice polarization.
item.dc:creator: Hong Li, Huandong Chen, Seongyeon Youn, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Trithep Devakul, Kazuhiro Fujita, Abhay Narayan Pasupathy

item.title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.07456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.
item.dc:creator: Zhenming Zhang, Tianyu Li, Wei Yi

item.title: Ultrafast Moir\'e Exciton Dynamics Revealed by Two-Dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.07539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices of van der Waals heterostructures confine excitons into discrete energy levels in finite-sized samples, yet their internal relaxation pathways remain obscured by inhomogeneous broadening. Here, using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS), we directly resolve seven discrete energy levels of the moir\'e-confined intralayer $\mathrm{WS}_{2}$ A exciton in an hBN-encapsulated $\mathrm{WS}_{2}/\mathrm{WSe}_{2}$ heterostructure, corresponding to a confinement depth of 57.02 meV. By tracking the population of these levels over picosecond delays, we uncover a two-stage thermalization process: an effective exciton temperature drops from 171.8 to 99.3 K within 1.2 ps through rapid intra-manifold population redistribution, followed by a slower recovery toward quasi-equilibrium mediated by exciton--environment interactions. Kullback--Leibler divergence analysis confirms the progressive transition from a non-equilibrium to a Boltzmann-distributed population. Our results establish state-resolved access to moir\'e exciton dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring nonequilibrium many-body phenomena in moir\'e quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Deran Zhang, Zhexue Chen, Dongxue Chen, Tengfei Yan, Jianhua Jiang, Hui Dong

item.title: Multi-Channel Non-Abelian Edge Pumping via Multi-Degeneracy Encircling
item.description: arXiv:2611.07594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Abelian operations enable sequence-dependent control of light, yet experimental realizations in wave systems have remained confined to local bulk or same-boundary modes and have often required fragile gap-closing degeneracies. Conventional Thouless pumps, meanwhile, support only two-channel edge transfer across a single gap. Here we demonstrate multi-channel non-Abelian edge pumping on a silicon photonic chip by adiabatically encircling multiple band degeneracies in a multi-gap lattice. In a minimal three-band band-triangle, two opposite-charge Weyl points and one zero-charge degeneracy are linked by global band connectivity, yielding both opposite-boundary and same-boundary edge channels. Sequencing these channels produces non-Abelian braiding of three topologically protected edge modes that reside on distinct physical boundaries. The process remains fully gapped and is protected by topological winding rather than by maintained spectral degeneracies. The same band-triangle principle extends systematically to an arbitrary number of channels, establishing a scalable route to collective, sequence-controlled routing of topological states in integrated photonic circuits.
item.dc:creator: Qingyang Mo, Jiacheng Sun, Zhongfu Li, Jiajun Li, Wange Song, Tao Li, Shuang Zhang

item.title: Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures
item.description: arXiv:2611.07807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonlinear interaction of closely spaced magnetic skyrmions remains poorly understood, particularly the conditions governing their merger into a single skyrmion or a stable skyrmionium. Here, we investigate the merging dynamics of two N\'eel skyrmions using analytical modelling and micromagnetic simulations based on Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. We examine the effects of exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, anisotropy, and magnetostatic energies by varying the initial separation, polarity, winding number, and skyrmion size. Our results reveal a topological selection rule: skyrmions with identical polarity and opposite winding numbers form a stable skyrmionium at intermediate overlap, while all other configurations relax into a single skyrmion. We also identify a critical radius below which the skyrmionium collapses, showing that its formation requires both the appropriate topology and a minimum size. Energy analysis reveals that the transition involves cooperative relaxation of exchange frustration and redistribution of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and magnetostatic energies, leading to a double-domain-wall structure. The resulting skyrmionium exhibits persistent breathing oscillations around an equilibrium radius, confirming its dynamical stability as a metastable state. These findings establish a predictive framework for controlling skyrmion merging and provide design guidelines for engineering skyrmionium textures in chiral magnetic nanostructures.
item.dc:creator: M. Al Busaidi, T. Hakioglu, R. Sbiaa

item.title: Signature of chiral anomaly in a graphene-based heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.07841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral anomaly is a fundamental manifestation of topological matter caused by chirality imbalance. It can be of great practical value by providing a mechanism for dissipationless transport. The phenomenon is highly sensitive to the system dimensionality, disappearing in the 2D limit. Different schemes have been proposed to observe the chiral anomaly in graphene-based systems but experimental evidence has been lacking. Here, we synthesized two types of the Gr/Sr/SiC nanostructure - with 2D and 3D, bulk-like, layers of Sr - the difference being the amount of Sr intercalated under graphene. In contrast to the 2D material, 3D Gr/Sr/SiC exhibits a signature of the chiral anomaly - quadratic negative magnetoresistance in parallel magnetic and electric fields. Also, the functional form of the temperature dependence of the magnetoresistance agrees with the chiral anomaly. In addition, the 3D heterostructure exhibits suppressed conductivity and quantum oscillations in graphene. These effects may be associated with the graphene layer incorporated into a complex 3D heterostructure. Hopefully, the discovered signature of chiral anomaly in the built-in graphene would spur research on the phenomenon in topological nanomaterials.
item.dc:creator: Ivan S. Sokolov, Dmitry V. Averyanov, Oleg E. Parfenov, Sergey P. Lebedev, Alexander A. Lebedev, Olesya O. Kapitanova, Alexey N. Mihalyuk, Oleg A. Kondratev, Andrey M. Tokmachev, Vyacheslav G. Storchak

item.title: Anisotropic g-tensor and strong spin-orbit interaction of holes in hexagonal germanium nanowires
item.description: arXiv:2611.07846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hexagonal germanium combines direct-gap optical activity with the low-nuclear-spin environment of a group-IV material, making it a candidate platform for spin qubits and spin-photon interfaces. Using a ten-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ model, we study the response of confined hole states in hexagonal germanium nanowires to magnetic and electric fields. We show that, by symmetry, the top valence band of the bulk crystal has a vanishing $g$ factor in the plane perpendicular to the $c$ axis, in analogy with the in-plane $g$ factor of heavy holes in two-dimensional hole gases. In nanowires, confinement induces only small transverse $g$-tensor components, so the $g$ tensor remains strongly anisotropic. A transverse electric field strongly reduces the nanowire band gap, providing a gate-tunable optical signature and limiting the usable field range. The same field induces a Rashba spin-orbit interaction that is markedly stronger for fields perpendicular to the $c$ axis and depends nonlinearly on the field strength. In narrow wires at strong fields, the spin-orbit length reaches a few tens of nanometers, comparable to hole devices in cubic silicon. We identify the microscopic origin of the Rashba coupling as a second-order process mediated by a few intermediate subbands with distinct symmetry selection rules. Our results provide guidance for the design of electrically controlled hole-spin qubits in hexagonal germanium nanowires.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Das, Baksa Kolok, D\'aniel Varjas, Andr\'as P\'alyi

item.title: When Molecular Dimerization Induces Magnetic Bi-Stability at the Metal-Organic Interface
item.description: arXiv:2611.08049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method to create metal-organic dimer complexes by on-surface assembly on a metal substrate using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS). We demonstrate that a dimer of Mn-Phthalocyanine (MnPc)2 on a Ag(111) surface can be switched between two stable configurations upon a small conformational change controlled by STM manipulation. By means of density-functional theory calculations, it is found that the two conformations correspond to an antiferromagnetic (AFM) and a ferromagnetic (FM) state respectively. Directly coordinated Mn atoms of the dimer lead to an AFM-coupling whereas indirectly coordinated (shifted) Mn atoms lead to a FM-coupling. Rarely seen in a molecular- dimers with transition-metal atoms, the FM-AFM-FM transition is thus readily on-surface accessible. Furthermore, the two configurations of the switch are easily identified by their Kondo states, opening interesting routes in terms of both, writing (FM versus AFM states) and reading. These results pave the experimental route toward dimer-based materials with complex magnetic structures of potential interest for application in spintronics, logics and computing.
item.dc:creator: Rouzhaji Tuerhong, Franck Ngassam, Mebarek Alouani, Jean-Pierre Bucher

item.title: Dynamical Keldysh model for colored noise and finite relaxation rate
item.description: arXiv:2611.08280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Keldysh model describes quantum dots subjected to Gaussian noise with infinite correlation time. For multi-component noise coupled through non-commuting matrices, the spectrum exhibits a pseudogap. We solve the model for coloured noise with any correlation time, $1/ \gamma$. Finite memory leads to the pseudogap being filled, its peaks merging and the line narrowing.
item.dc:creator: F. Z. Bendjeddou, D. V. Efremov, M. N. Kiselev

item.title: Anisotropy lifts topological protection of transport in pumped spin chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.08385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the prospect of topological spin pumping and transport in a dimerized spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ anisotropic XY chain with tunable in-plane anisotropy. Through a Jordan-Wigner transformation, the system maps onto an extended Rice-Mele-type fermionic model whose momentum-space band structure exhibits gapped regions characterized by nonzero Chern numbers ($\pm 1$) as well as trivial and gapless regimes. Conventional momentum-space analysis therefore predicts quantized Thouless-type spin pumping in parts of the Chern number diagram. However, real-space time evolution under open boundary conditions reveals that the spin transport is generally not quantized away from the isotropic limit. In the anisotropic regime, eigen-energy states within the transporting subspace hybridize during the driving cycle, leading to a transport that depends on details of the driving protocol. Quantized pumping and transport survive only in the isotropic limit, where the Hamiltonian reduces to decoupled Rice-Mele sectors and the transported spin component is conserved. Our results demonstrate that momentum-space topological invariants alone do not guarantee quantized spin transport in anisotropic spin chains. More broadly, they show that the conventional Thouless-pumping framework does not straightforwardly extend to situations where the transported quantity is not conserved, highlighting the importance of real-space diagnostics in topological transport phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Mainak Pal

item.title: Synaptic Multi-Weight Wafer-Scale Domain Wall Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Driven by Spin Orbit Torque
item.description: arXiv:2611.08405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spintronic synaptic devices based on magnetic random access memory (MRAM) are a rapidly evolving class within the analog neuromorphic architecture. However, obtaining the multi-weight or analog behavior desired for improved neural network inference accuracy in scaled MRAM remains a challenge. In this study, we demonstrate and tune up to eight distinct resistance levels in 300 mm wafer-scale magnetic tunnel junction artificial synapses driven by spin orbit torque. By varying the applied in-plane field, multi-weight resistance states emerge through domain wall nucleation and pinning. These multi-weight states appear stochastically and can be addressed with an iterative programming algorithm to program a specific resistance. Electromagnetic simulations indicate the multiple states are due to domain wall nucleation mediated by in-plane field and applied voltage. Implementation of the measured multi-weight devices in a neural network yields a 96.1% inference accuracy using the MNIST dataset if all devices provide the same number of multi-weight states. When experimental device-to-device variation is included, the accuracy is 48.6%. Overall, this work demonstrates a route towards multi-weight artificial synapse MRAM, establishing a path towards scalable neuromorphic systems based on spintronics.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Zogbi, Domenico Giuliano, Vaishnavi Kateel, Van Dai Nguyen, Jyotirmoy Chatterjee, Alvaro Palomino, Robert Carpenter, Siddharth Rao, Jean Anne C. Incorvia

item.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two-dimensional charge-density field. The desired spatial distribution of the confined charge defines the target quantum-dot geometry for inverse design. The FNO reproduces charge densities with a relative $L^2$ test error of just 0.6\% and enables millisecond-scale differentiable evaluations. Relative to the CPU-based physics simulator, the FNO achieves a 17,000-fold speed-up on GPU for a single design, with further performance gains enabled by batched inference. When embedded in a gradient-based design loop with fabrication constraints, the FNO can produce both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions. The ability to engineer these distinct confinement configurations demonstrates control over quantum-dot shape and position, providing a route towards designing devices with distinct qubit-relevant operating properties prior to fabrication.
item.dc:creator: Marek Rychetsky, Valentin Duruisseaux, Freya Shah, David L. Craig, Ming Ni, Georgios Katsaros, Taylor L. Patti, Anima Anandkumar, Natalia Ares

item.title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.07036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase \pi/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Musolino, Daniele Lamberto, Salvatore Savasta, Federico Roccati

item.title: Universal Negative Correlation between Nonreciprocity and Superconducting Transition Width in FeTe-Based Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.07116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport in noncentrosymmetric superconductors probes broken symmetries and superconducting fluctuations and underpins the superconducting diode effect. Despite extensive studies, the factors governing its magnitude remain unclear. In this work, we use molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to synthesize a broad family of FeTe-based superconducting heterostructures with top layers spanning topologically trivial versus nontrivial, layered versus nonlayered, and magnetic versus nonmagnetic materials. Through systematic first- and second-harmonic transport measurements, we find that the magnetochiral anisotropy coefficient $\gamma$ is insensitive to the top-layer crystal structure, lattice constant, thickness, topology, and magnetism, but exhibits a negative correlation with the superconducting transition width $\Delta T$. Control measurements on superconducting stoichiometric FeTe films reveal much weaker nonreciprocity, confirming the essential role of interfacial inversion-symmetry breaking. Combined with a disorder-based theoretical model, our results establish a universal relationship: for comparable inversion-symmetry breaking, reduced interfacial disorder sharpens the superconducting transition and strongly enhances nonreciprocal transport in the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition regime. These findings identify $\Delta T$ as a unifying parameter governing nonreciprocity across FeTe-based heterostructures, reconcile previously disparate observations, and establish a general framework for engineering enhanced nonreciprocal superconducting responses and exploring superconducting diode effects in nonlinear quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Annie G. Wang, Saswata Mandal, Zi-Jie Yan, Bomin Zhang, Xiaoda Liu, Hongtao Rong, Deyi Zhuo, Pu Xiao, Lok-Kan Lai, Zhiyuan Xi, Ke Wang, Chao-Xing Liu, Cui-Zu Chang

item.title: Electrically tunable superconducting dimensionality in stripe-ordered monolayer MoTe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dimensionality governs the stability of collective quantum states, including whether Cooper pairs can establish the phase coherence required for superconductivity. In solids, however, electronic dimensionality is usually encoded in the crystal structure and is difficult to control reversibly. Here we show evidence that monolayer 1$T^{\prime}$-MoTe$_2$ develops a stripe charge-density wave that reorganizes its low-energy electronic states into quasi-one-dimensional channels. Raman spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy identify the stripe order, whereas directional transport and tunneling spectroscopy reveal superconducting correlations confined to the stripe direction and insulating behavior perpendicular to it. Electrostatic doping weakens the transverse insulating response and drives the system into phase-coherent two-dimensional superconductivity. These results show that stripe charge order can reconfigure superconducting dimensionality and make it electrically tunable within a single crystalline layer.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Qiu, Ziyi Han, Fei Yang, Keyu Wei, Liguo Dou, Yong Zhang, Dekun Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xuefeng Wang, Fucong Fei, Fengqi Song, Yanyan Shangguan, Shaochun Li, Jinsheng Wen, Hong Yao, Chaoxing Liu, Binghai Yan, Lin He, Xiaoxiang Xi

item.title: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($\Xi$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $\Xi$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. Within this framework, in the $\Xi$ manifold of hBN-encapsulated WSe$_2$, a weak optical pulse, preceded by a terahertz pulse in the counterintuitive STIRAP order, converts the excitation it creates into an optically dark exciton by dark-state following, while the lossy bright intermediate exciton stays nearly empty. The conversion is limited by emission from that intermediate state rather than by non-adiabatic coupling, and is controlled by a single adiabaticity parameter of the terahertz leg. The exchange mean field of the exciton gas shifts the two-photon resonance by more than the conversion tolerates at moderate densities; the center of the cascade transparency window provides an in situ calibration, and we identify the control strengths at which it is true EIT rather than Autler--Townes splitting. The $V$ manifold loses its coherence on the radiative timescale and serves as the unprotected reference. These results provide a minimal, material-specific baseline for dark-state coherent control of excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors in the radiative limit.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Martinez, Martin A. Mosquera

item.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
item.description: arXiv:2611.07401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.
item.dc:creator: Motohiko Ezawa

item.title: Discrete quadrature spectrum of composite bosons: Weyl relation, intensity correlations, and binned homodyne detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.07776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A composite boson made of two fermions can look elementary under one measurement and composite under another. In an exactly solvable paired-mode model we compare three probes: classical drives, periodically binned quadrature statistics, and intensity correlations $g^{(2)}$. The Weyl defect has an exact product formula and a controlled dilute expansion in the Schmidt moments. The binned observables are instead piecewise constant in the Schmidt weights and sensitive to single eigenvalues crossing bin edges; on the flat-spectrum ladder they converge slowly and nonmonotonically over the computed range. A spectral filter and a polar correction recover an exact Pauli algebra; a heralded joint projection then extracts a logical singlet from the vacua of two independent copies of the composite, with probability set by the accepted weight and the mixedness of the filtered reduced qubit. Finite-mode examples with Schmidt number about three succeed at the percent level despite order-one Weyl defects; near-unit $g^{(2)}$ does not control the binned algebra. For flat spectra the construction converges strongly to its oscillator counterpart, whose vacuum overlap is strictly positive at every scale; for infinite spectra with summable Schmidt amplitudes it converges at all but countably many filter cutoffs, positivity at the cutoffs studied remaining open.
item.dc:creator: Itzhak Roditi

item.title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ via non-magnetic extension
item.description: arXiv:2611.07844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ in contact with non-magnetic GeBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Bi$_2$Te$_3$) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.
item.dc:creator: Igor P. Rusinov, Tatiana V. Menshchikova, Evgueni V. Chulkov

item.title: Continuum Photonic Axion Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.07893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Here, I study the conditions for realizing an axion topology in a homogeneous inversion-symmetric electromagnetic continuum, in the absence of a crystalline lattice. I introduce a continuum inversion invariant expressed solely in terms of the spectral properties of the material response in the zero- and infinite-wave-vector limits. Surprisingly, it is found that standard gyrotropic-type material responses are strongly constrained and, under fairly general conditions, cannot open an axion gap within first-order perturbation theory. Based on an analogy between the effective response of crystalline photonic axion insulators and the optical response of centrosymmetric altermagnets, a class of spatially dispersive odd magnetoelectric couplings that can open an axion gap is identified. These findings suggest an interesting hierarchy of nonreciprocal mechanisms in electromagnetic continua: while uniform gyrotropy relates to Chern phases, odd magnetoelectric coupling relates to axion phases.
item.dc:creator: Mario G. Silveirinha

item.title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.08019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.
item.dc:creator: Yang Li, Zuzhang Lin, Zhikuan Wang, Chengzhi Wu, Zeyu Jiang, Bing Huang

item.title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
item.description: arXiv:2611.08051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.
item.dc:creator: Ji\v{r}\'i Janek, Miriam Mago\v{c}iov\'a, Alexandr Malijevsk\'y

item.title: Coupling between molecular exchange qubits
item.description: arXiv:2611.08058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin triangles are promising systems for defining and manipulating scalar degrees of freedom, such as chirality, partial spin sums, or combinations between the two. Here we extend this analysis to dimers formed by pairs of spin triangles, coupled by exchange or dipolar interactions. We show that the weak-coupling limit warrants the introduction of an effective two-qubit picture, and derive the expressions of the related Hamiltonians as a function of the underlying physical interaction between the triangles. We benchmark this two-qubit Hamiltonian against the microscopic one, and discuss the observable effects of the inter-triangle coupling on the spin-electric transitions between states with different chiralities or partial-spin sums.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Troiani, Jason S. R. McCoombs, Athanassios K. Boudalis

item.title: Gate-tunable Josephson parametric amplifiers based on semiconductor nanowires
item.description: arXiv:2510.00305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor hybrid materials have been extensively used for experiments on electrically tunable quantum devices. Notably, Josephson junctions utilizing nanowire weak links have enabled a number of new gate-tunable qubits, including gatemons, Andreev level qubits and spin qubits. Conversely, superconducting parametric amplifiers based on Josephson junctions have not yet been implemented using nanowires, even though such nearly quantum limited amplifiers are key elements in experiments on quantum circuits. Here we present Josephson parametric amplifiers based on arrays of parallel InAs nanowires that feature a large critical current as required for linear amplification. The resonance frequency of the devices is gate-tunable by almost 1 GHz, with a gain exceeding 20 dB in multiple frequencies and markedly improved noise performance compared to a low-temperature commercial amplifier. This platform enables on-chip integration of gate-tunable qubits with nearly quantum limited amplifiers using the same hybrid materials and on any substrate.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Rousset-Zenou, Nicolas Aparicio, Simon Messelot, Rasmus D. Schlosser, Martin Bjergfelt, Julien Renard, Mo\"ira Hocevar, Jesper Nyg{\aa}rd

item.title: Conductivity of charge-neutral multicomponent 2D electron-hole system
item.description: arXiv:2604.07846v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interplay between distinct carrier species in systems with broken Galilean invariance can give rise to a rich landscape of interaction-driven transport phenomena. Here, we develop a comprehensive theory of the electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional mixture of massless Dirac and massive fermions, a system realized in HgTe quantum wells tuned to the charge-neutrality point. In this regime, all carriers are thermally activated, enabling a self-consistent, temperature-dependent interplay between the two species. Crucially, the charge-neutrality condition ensures that the chemical potential is not externally pinned but is determined self-consistently, thereby making the system's transport response an intrinsic probe of inter-species quantum friction. We demonstrate that the conductivity changes with temperature : at low temperatures, transport is dominated by massless Dirac carriers, yielding a nearly temperature-independent conductivity reminiscent of the charge-neutrality point in pristine graphene. As the temperature rises, massive holes become thermally excited, and their mutual scattering with Dirac carriers induces a specific nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the conductivity in both clean and disordered structures. In particular, in nearly clean structures with strong screening modeled by a short-range interparticle interaction potential, the system's conductivity can exhibit an inverse-quadratic temperature dependence. Conversely, in disordered structures with a long-range interparticle interaction, it varies quadratically with temperature. Our findings establish HgTe quantum wells at charge neutrality as a clean, highly tunable platform for isolating and quantitatively studying interaction-driven transport in the absence of Galilean invariance, offering a direct pathway to explore regimes where interparticle collisions dominate over disorder.
item.dc:creator: Yuping Huang, O. V. Kibis, V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko

item.title: Singlet-only always-on gapless exchange (SAGE) spin qubits: Charge noise effects and two-qubit gates
item.description: arXiv:2604.15419v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Singlet-only always-on gapless exchange (SAGE) spin qubits are an alternative type of exchange-only (EO) qubits that encode a single qubit in the spins of four electrons located in four tunnel-coupled quantum dots. While conventional EO qubits are susceptible to local magnetic field gradients caused by local nuclear environments and $g$-factor variations, the SAGE qubit subspace is inherently protected from magnetic-gradient-induced Pauli errors by virtue of the singlet-only encoding, which is invariant under magnetic field gradients, and the always-on exchange couplings, which provide energetic leakage protection. However, the always-on operation simultaneously increases the qubit's sensitivity to charge noise. Here, starting from a Hubbard model describing the underlying electronic structure of the coupled quantum dots, we characterize the performance of SAGE qubits in the presence of $1/f$ charge noise that induces fluctuations in both the dot chemical potentials and the interdot tunnel couplings. We calculate SAGE idle coherence times and show that realistic CPMG-like pulse sequences can be used to significantly extend SAGE single-qubit coherence times for experimentally relevant charge noise strengths. We likewise study the fidelity of SAGE two-qubit gates in the presence of charge and magnetic noise and again propose a simple refocusing strategy to mitigate the noise, while increased ramp times of the entangling pulse suppress leakage into noncomputational states.
item.dc:creator: Nathan L. Foulk, Katharina Laubscher, Silas Hoffman, Sankar Das Sarma

item.title: Thermal bottleneck in a freely suspended superconducting island on InAs nanowire
item.description: arXiv:2605.03139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the heat balance in superconducting islands (S-islands) formed in epitaxial Al/InAs nanowires (NWs) freely suspended above the substrate. We employ a Joule spectroscopy approach, which traces the superconductor-normal transition in the S-island mediated by heating of the neighboring InAs NW segments via transport current. The temperature of the surrounding 3He bath is varied with nearby mesoscopic heaters and controlled with the NW Johnson noise thermometry. The experiment reveals a substantial thermal relaxation bottleneck associated with the cooling via surrounding 3He, which gives rise to phonon heating in the S-island. Our results uncover the role of environmental cooling in non-equilibrium experiments in S-islands in NW devices.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Shpagina, E. S. Tikhonov, D. Ruhstorfer, G. Koblmueller, V. S. Khrapai

item.title: Reflective Metastructure Q-plate for Ultrashort Laser Pulses
item.description: arXiv:2606.12041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The orbital angular momentum of light is an intriguing property for developing light driven applications. It emerged as an independent degree of freedom by which to manipulate light and, consequently, the interaction of light with matter. Several methods exist for the generation of light carrying orbital angular momentum, mostly employing transmitting or reflecting optical components, which radially modulate the phase profile of the light. As one of such components, transmissive q-plates established themselves as standard elements due to their usability over a broad wavelength range. Here, we present our approach to building a highly reflective q-plate with a diameter of 4.5 mm based on a plasmonic metasurface capable of converting orbital angular momentum from the nanostructure to ultrashort laser pulses without measurable temporal broadening under the investigated conditions. We highlight its working principle over a wide range of wavelengths for reflection under normal and grazing incidence.
item.dc:creator: Christopher G. O. Wei{\ss}, Ellen Brennfleck, Bert L\"agel, Laurenz Rettig, Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann, Tobias Eul

item.title: Generalized Fourier's law in mesoscopic systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.23909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fourier's law fails when the mean free path of the energy carriers becomes comparable to the length and time scales over which the temperature field varies. We derive a thermodynamically consistent generalization in which the conductivity becomes a nonlocal memory operator $\mathbf{\kappa}_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{k},\omega)$, by combining mesoscopic nonequilibrium thermodynamics with the Mori--Kubo--Zwanzig projection-operator formalism. The Onsager kernel is a tensor sum over vibrational normal modes weighted by their Bose heat capacities and relaxation functions; it satisfies the second law for any closure consistent with the fluctuation--dissipation theorem and reduces, in the relaxation-time closure, to the nonlocal conductivity of the phonon Boltzmann equation. Two consequences follow. First, direction-dependent sampling of this tensor in a pump--probe experiment makes a nominally isotropic crystal exhibit apparent conductivities $\Lambda_z\neq\Lambda_r$. Second, the modulation frequency does not introduce temporal memory but sets the probed wavevector through the thermal penetration depth, so that the frequency-dependent suppression of the apparent conductivity measured by time-domain thermoreflectance on Ge and SiGe alloys is a spatial-nonlocality effect, with effective lengths of $0.25$--$0.4~\mu$m. With published mean-free-path spectra and no parameter adjusted to the thermoreflectance data, the kernel reproduces the spot-size dependence of Si, the frequency dependence of the apparent conductivity of Ge and Si$_{0.2}$Ge$_{0.8}$ and the rise of the apparent interface conductance of Al/Si$_{0.99}$Ge$_{0.01}$, and contains the two-channel ballistic/diffusive model as a two-sector projection.
item.dc:creator: Luciano C. Lapas (Latin American Institute of Life and Natural Sciences, Universidade Federal da Integra\c{c}\~ao Latino-Americana, Foz do Igua\c{c}u, PR, Brazil)

item.title: Specific absorption rate of uniaxial single-domain nanomagnets: stochastic spin dynamics versus linear response theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.27351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the specific absorption rate of a uniaxial single-domain nanomagnet driven by an alternating magnetic field by two methods: i) direct numerical integration of the stochastic (Langevin) Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation (the LLL approach), and ii) linear response theory (LRT) based on the Debye susceptibility with the N\'eel relaxation time $\ta$. We first analytically show that both methods are equivalent for small magnetic field amplitude, and then compute their deviation $\Lambda\equiv\SAR_{\LLL}/\SAR_{\LRT}-1$ as a function of the magnetic field amplitude for two temperatures chosen on opposite sides of the Debye resonance. One of the main results is that the sign and magnitude of $\Lambda$ are governed by the dimensionless product $\om\ta$, in addition to the linearity parameter $\xi=\mu_{s}B_{0}/k_{B}T$ for the easy-axis geometry considered here. Indeed, below resonance ($\om\ta<1$), linear response theory overestimates the specific absorption rate, whereas above resonance ($\om\ta>1$, the regime typical of blocked nanoparticles) linear response theory can underestimate the specific absorption rate by up to $\sim70\%$ at $\xi\sim2$. We expect this work to provide a quantitative guidance for the use of linear response theory in magnetic hyperthermia and related nanoscale heat-transport problems, and to serve as a single-particle benchmark for extensions to many-spin and interacting systems.
item.dc:creator: H. Kachkachi

item.title: Monte Carlo solution of the Kondo model
item.description: arXiv:2607.07797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kondo model is a paradigmatic quantum impurity problem realized in a wide variety of experimental platforms and central to the study of strongly correlated electrons. We introduce a discrete model that exactly reproduces the multichannel Kondo model and demonstrate that it can be simulated efficiently. Using cluster Monte Carlo algorithms, we completely eliminate critical slowing down, providing direct access to universal crossover functions and transport properties across a broad range of parameters. Remarkably, the same model captures both the weak- and strong-coupling regimes, unifying descriptions traditionally derived in complementary limits and revealing their common origin. Our method naturally accommodates large channel numbers, anisotropy, interacting one-dimensional leads, and channel asymmetry, yielding predictions for transport properties in charge-Kondo devices.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Paris, Oscar Bouverot-Dupuis, Christophe Mora

item.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.41414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

item.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.41419v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

item.title: Statistical properties of quantum jumps between macroscopic states of light: reading an operational coherence record
item.description: arXiv:2512.07754v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose an experimental apparatus to reveal the quantum coherence manifested in downward quantum jumps of amplitude bistability. The underlying coherent superposition of macroscopic quantum states is translated into the statistical properties of the integrated charge deposited in the detector circuit of a mode-matched heterodyne/homodyne detection scheme. At first, the dynamical evolution of a signal transmitted from an auxiliary cavity is employed to pinpoint a macroscopic switching event in a bistable main cavity subject to direct photodetection. Once the decision is made on the occurrence of a downward switch, the main cavity mode is let to freely decay to the vacuum, monitored to the production of an integrated charge. In the long-time limit, the charge distribution over an identical collection of pure states generated during the jumps converges to the Q function (heterodyne detection) or marginals of the Wigner function (homodyne detection) dictated by the phase of the local oscillator. When fluctuations over the ensemble step in, we connect the statistical properties of several switching events and the ensuing production of current records, to the cavity field correlations associated with the breakdown of photon blockade.
item.dc:creator: Th. K. Mavrogordatos

item.title: Chiral vortical effect and boundary-induced vortical pumping in finite Weyl systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.01293v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The chiral vortical effect (CVE) -- an axial current driven by rotation in chiral matter -- appears in systems ranging from relativistic fluids to Weyl semimetals. We present a quantum treatment of a rotating Weyl fermion in a finite cylinder that reproduces the on-axis current density obtained by Vilenkin in an infinite system, while revealing two new phenomena. First, we find that the cross-sectional averaged current density vanishes in the thermodynamic limit, establishing that the bulk vortical response is purely a magnetization current. Second, for spin-polarized boundary conditions, we uncover a robust family of chiral modes that transport axial charge, $\Delta Q=\chi N^2\Delta\theta/4\pi$, under rotation by angle $\Delta\theta$, where $\chi$ is the Weyl node chirality and $N$ is the number of chiral modes. The pump is independent of temperature, Fermi level, and Weyl velocities, but depends on the UV-sensitive number $N$. These results clarify the quantum structure of the bulk CVE and reveal a boundary-enforced chiral spectral structure underlying vortical response in Weyl systems.
item.dc:creator: B. Q. Song, Pavan Hosur

item.title: Topological metal-insulator transitions in one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasicrystals: beyond PT-symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2605.25072v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One-dimensional non-Hermitian quasicrystals with parity and time-reversal (PT) symmetry can simultaneously exhibit localization-delocalization transition, topological phase transition, and PT-symmetry-breaking transition. This motivates us to investigate how the absence of PT symmetry impacts topological metal-insulator transitions in non-Hermitian quasicrystals. We propose a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model that generally does not preserve PT-symmetry but, in most parameter regions, hosts a generic triple-transition scenario encompassing localization, topological, and degeneracy-breaking transitions. These transitions can be understood within the dual momentum-space representation featuring asymmetric couplings. Specifically, the localization boundary is obtained from the dual momentum-space representation by comparing the Lyapunov exponent, or inverse localization length, of the reciprocal Aubry-Andr\'e model with the nonreciprocal hopping-asymmetry ratio of the dual lattice. The accompanying topological transition is characterized by a point-gap winding number defined with respect to a reference energy inside the complex spectral gap, whereas the degeneracy-breaking transition is understood from the loss of the reciprocal $n\leftrightarrow -n$ spectral symmetry. The system also exhibits a localization-delocalization transition analogous to that in the Hermitian case, which occurs without accompanying topological or degeneracy-breaking transitions. Our work extends the topological metal-insulator transitions previously studied in PT-symmetric systems to a more general class of non-Hermitian setting, and further reveals that non-Hermitian systems can host distinct types of localization behavior.
item.dc:creator: Guangjie Zhang, Bing Shao, Longwen Zhou, Jiangbin Gong, Weiwei Zhu

item.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.15749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

item.title: Layer-Parity Control of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Monolayer NbSe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-$\mathbf Q$ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe$_2$. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which $C_3$ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}=0$ yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above $0.65$~meV at $0.58$~K. Magnetic layer parity thus selects between a helical and a trigonal diode channel. This trigonal channel provides a candidate intrinsic contribution to the field-free rectification reported in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$. The model predicts that two-sided out-of-plane proximity cancels it when antiparallel and, at the same exchange per layer, enhances it about fourfold when parallel, in the computed range.
item.dc:creator: Yusuf Wicaksono, Toshikaze Kariyado
